114.  The Committee notes the reply and desires that the response of the State Government on the above
 recommendations may be obtained on priority and a detailed study on the response may be forwarded to the
 Committee for further action.
(Recommendation at Para 142)
115. The Committee understands that the Indian Railways has adopted an aggressive marketing strategy for
 increasing its share of freight traffic. The Committee is at a loss to understand as to why there is no initiative to
 upgrade the design parameters of the roads commensurating with the technological advancement in the load
 carriers enabling them to bear higher load capacities. The Committee is of the view that this has resulted in the
 flouting of provisions related to overloading. The Committee notes that the Department has held that the
 revenue likely to accrue on account of increase in Gross Vehicle Weight will be accrued to the State
 Governments and Central Government will not get any part thereof. Further, on the one hand it is submitted by
 them that the likely increase in revenue is not possible to assess, on the other hand it is claimed that the loss
 caused on account of the deterioration of roads would be much more than the revenue that would be gained by
 the State Governments. The Committee also feels that non-accrual of any revenue to the Central Government by
 way of road tax consequent on the increase in the permissible Gross Vehicle Weight should not be taken as an
 excuse to defer the decision on the suitable amendments to the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988. The Committee expects
 that the Department will either ensure the strict compliance of provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 or
 consider the amendment in the Act to help the carriage sector.
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT
116.  The Department held a meeting of technical experts regarding implications of revision of the Gross Vehicle
 Weight (GVW). Unanimous opinion of the experts was that any increase in GVW while keeping the road design
 parameters unchanged would have a disastrous consequence on the life and maintainability of road infrastructure. On
 the other hand, changing the design parameters of the road and increase in GVW is going to be unaffordable and
 expensive. Further, it also came out that GVW legislated in India is comparable to the rest of the world. The
 Department has, however, decided to commission a study through Central Road Research Institute (CRRI) for in-depth
 examination of all issues pertaining to overloading and possibility, if any, of revision of GVW.
(Recommendation at Para 147)
117.  The Committee is surprised to note that even though the Integrated Transport Policy was formulated in the
 year 2001, the National Road Transport Policy has not been finalised so far. The Committee further notes that
 the discussions on the draft National Road Transport Policy are still in preliminary stage and meetings with
 stakeholders are still to be held. Further, the agency to be entrusted the task of submitting a revised draft has
 not been finalised. In this scenario, the Committee is apprehensive that the National Road Transport Policy
 document will not be available by December, 2006 as envisaged. The Committee recommends that concerted
 efforts should be made to finalise the National Road Transport Policy expeditiously. In this context, the
 Committee had observed in its 84th Report that the absence of the right kind of modal-mix in the country is
 hampering optimum utilisation of all the resources. The Committee therefore reiterates its recommendations
 made in the same Report that the Government must come forward with an integrated transport policy to make
 optimum utilisation of the various transport facilities available in the country.
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT
118.  The Integrated Transport Policy comes under the purview of Planning Commission. This Department is in the
 process of finalization of an agency to assist the Department in drafting National Road Transport Policy. The National
 Road Transport Policy is expected to be ready by March, 2007. The same would be sent to the Planning Commission
 for incorporation in Integrated Transport Policy.
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
119.  A copy of the text of the National Road Transport Policy should be furnished to the Committee for its
 perusal as and when it is finalised by the Department.
(Recommendation at Para 148)
120.  The Committee was informed that recently the Ministry of Finance has issued instructions vide
 F.No.7/16/2004-1 FU(B&A) dated the 8th December, 2004 wherein it has been impressed upon to all
 Ministry/Department that 67 per cent of the budgetary allocations should be spent upto December and rest of
 the 33 per cent of the budgetary allocations could spent in the last quarter ending March. However, ceiling of the
 budgeted expenditure cannot be observed in the Department of Road Transport and Highways since most of the
 construction work starts after the monsoon season. The Committee notes that the problem faced by the

 explained the reasons for not sanctioning any new work under this scheme during the year 2006-07 despite being

         The Committee is not satisfied with the reply of the Department of Road Transport and Highways that slow
 progress in the implementation of National Highways (Land and Traffic) Act, 2002 is due to the problems

 the matter immediately with the Ministry of Finance to resolve the impasse in the non-accrual of previous fund

 committee also pointed out that the pattern of distribution of accrual from Central Road Fund is not equitable
 and despite the enhanced allocation received during the year 2006-07, the share granted to State Roads and
 centrally Sponsored Schemes have not increased in comparison to 2005-06 and in case of rural roads it has been

REPORT
        The Report of the Committee deals with the Action Taken by the Government on the observations
 recommendations as contained in its One Hundred and Third Report on Demands for Grants  (2006-07) (Demand No.
 20) of the Department of Culture, which was presented to the Parliament on  22nd May, 2007.
2.     Action Taken Replies have been received from the Government on 15th January 2007 in respect of all the
 observations/recommendations contained in the Report. These have been categorized as follows:-
 (i) Recommendations/observations that have been accepted by the Government:  
  Para Nos. 11, 15, 21, 29, 37, 55 and 61 Total-7
 (ii) Recommendations/observations which the Committee does not desire to pursue in
 view of the Government replies:
 
  Para No. 65 Total-1
 (iii) Recommendations/observations in respect of which replies of the Government have
 not been accepted by the Committee:
 
  Para Nos. 32 and 49 Total-2
 (iv) Recommendations/observations in respect of which final replies of the Government
 are still awaited:
 
  Para Nos. 18, 24, 40, 44 and 71 Total-5
3.     The Committee desires that final replies in respect of the recommendations, which have been categorized as
 interim replies by the Committee should be furnished to it at the earliest.
4.     On scrutiny of the said Action Taken Replies, the Committee has made observations on each item of the action
 taken/proposed to be taken by the Ministry. The recommendations of the Committee contained in the One Hundred and
 Third, action taken thereon by the Government and recommendations/observations of the Committee on each item of
 action taken have been given in the succeeding paragraphs.
THE APPROACH IN THE TENTH PLAN AND ANALYSIS OF THE ANNUAL PLAN 2005-06
(Recommendation at Para 11)
5.     The Committee is of the view that fixing of the Revised Estimates ceiling by the Ministry of Finance on the
 basis of the level of expenditure attained upto the month of September/October creates problem for the
 Department of Culture. The Committee observes that most of the cultural functions and festivals take place in
 the month of October and November, after the monsoon. The Archaeological Survey of India also incurres
 major expenditure after the monsoon. The Committee, therefore, recommends that Government must review
 the budgeting procedure and evolve some mechanism to ensure that the Plan allocation for the Department of
 Culture is not reduced. The Committee recommends that if the review of the budgetary allocation is done in the
 month of December, instead of the month of September then the cut in the budgetary provision could be
 avoided. The Committee observes that the major allocation for conservation work is being done under Non Plan
 Allocation. The Committee, therefore, recommends that conversation activity should be brought under the Plan
 Head so that conservation is not affected for want of funds, which is causing problem to the Department of
 Culture who wish to increase the conservation activities, hence need more expenditure.
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT
6.     In pursuance of the recommendation of the Parliamentary Standing Committee, budget provision for conservation
 will be brought under Plan heads while preparing the Budget Estimates for 2007-08 onwards.
7.     In Archaeological Survey of India, field officers are asked regularly to programme  the activities in such a manner
 that flow of expenditure is proportionately distributed in the months and 67 per cent expenditure is achieved by end of
 December. But as the conservation work of Archaeological Survey of India is seasonal in nature and in extreme
 summer and monsoon seasons, the pace of work and the flow of expenditure will be slow and the flow of expenditure
 will not strictly be proportionate every month. Archaeological survey of India is explaining the above to Planning
 Commission and Ministry of Culture every year to minimize the budget reduction on this ground.
8.     With regard to review of Budgetary  allocation in the month of December instead of September, the
 recommendations of the Committee have been forwarded to Ministry of Finance and Planning Commission for

 obtaining their comments/decision.
ARCHAEOLOGICAL SURVEY OF INDIA
(a)    Release of the Revenue Collected as Admission Fees to Archaeological Survey of India
(Recommendation at Para 15)
9.     The Committee feels that execution of conservation and preservation works need an expertise and timely
 funding of projects. But with its meager resource, it is difficult for the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) to
 protect and maintain all the 3667 monuments/sites. The Committee, therefore, recommends that 100 per cent of
 the revenue collected as entry fees from ticketed monuments should be released to ASI for stepping up the
 activities and to augment resources of ASI. Coordinated efforts should also be taken by the Department to bring
 more monuments under central protection and also efforts should be made to raise the number of monuments
 for ticketing purpose to generate more revenue. The Committee strongly feels that there exists a requirement for
 creation of a non lapsable fund out of the amount generated by the ticketing of monuments which can be used
 for preservation and development of monuments in a dedicated manner.
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT
10.   A proposal for creation of a Non-lapsable fund for conservation and preservation activities on National monuments
 of Archaeological Survey of India, out of revenue obtained by sale of entry ticket was made to Ministry of Finance
 after consultation with Deputy Chairman, Planning Commission. In this regard the Minister for Tourism and Culture
 had written to Minister of Finance vide letter dated 3.9.2005. Ministry of Finance, Department of Economic Affairs
 vide their letter dated 27.12.2005 had asked for further details which were furnished by Archaeological Survey of India
 vide letter dated 16.3.2006. The proposal is now under consideration of Ministry of Finance, Department of Economic
 Affairs.
11.   In the year 1999 the total number of protected monuments was 3597 while now it has increased to 3667. Though
 the manpower resources of Archaeological Survey of India is a limiting factor in taking more monuments for central
 protection, Archaeological Survey of India continues to take more monuments of outstanding architectural/historical
 importance for protection under the Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains Act, 1958. All field
 officers have been directed to review the number of ticketed monuments with the objective of bringing more
 monuments under ticketing.
(b)    The Post of Director-General in Archaeological Survey of India (ASI)
(Recommendation at Para 18)
12.   The Committee regrets to note that the promotional post of ADG, ASI could not be filled up as there was no
 suitable candidate in the country and ultimately the post was abolished as per the rules/regulations of the
 Department of Expenditure because the post could not be filled within prescribed time limit. It is pity that we
 are having more than hundred year old premier institute like ASI, but there is no archaeologist to be fit for
 promotion to the post of ADG. It clearly shows the callous attitude of the Government so far as management of
 the affairs of ASI is concerned. The Committee is of the view that there is no dearth of talent in the country.
 However, there is need to do away the rigidity in the eligibility criteria for the posts of Joint Director General,
 ADG and then DG, ASI. The Committee hopes that the vacant post will be filled up at the earliest as promised
 by the Secretary during the course of his evidence.
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT
13.   The post of Additional Director General (Archaeology) is the only feeder post which provides promotional avenues
 to the departmental officers for the post of Director General in the Archaeological Survey of India. The post of
 Additional Director General (Archaeology) in the Archaeological Survey of India has already been revived and the
 UPSC has been asked to fill up the post.
FURTHER RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATION OF THE COMMITTEE
14.   The Committee notes the reply of the Ministry and hopes that UPSC will take due care to fill up the vacant
 post at the earliest. The Committee however, hopes that recruitment condition for the post of Additional
 Director General (Archaeology) must have been framed taking into account the availability of manpower in this
 connection so that there are enough candidates available for the post.
(c)    Conservation and Preservation of Monuments by the ASI

15.   The Committee is happy to note that more and more corporate houses are coming forward to help the ASI
 in conservation of monuments by way of contributions to National Culture Fund. The Committee recommends
 that the Department of Culture should continue its efforts to ensure more involvement of private sector
 companies/firms. But at the same time the Committee also cautions that private involvement should not lead to
 commercial use of the monuments putting their safety and sanctity at stake.
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT
16.   The National Culture Fund (NCF) was constituted as a Trust in 1996 for infusion of private and corporate capital
 for cultural activities. Several projects have been initiated under NCF for conservation, preservation and environmental
 development of heritage monuments which are protected by the Archaeological Survey of India.
17.   Under the prevailing scheme, Archaeological Survey of India enters into an MoU with the National Culture Fund
 and the private/public sector company for taking up projects of conservation and preservation of monuments. The
 provisions of the MoU would detail conditions under which the projects are taken up, and due care is always taken to
 ensure that there would be no commercialization of the monuments and the safety and sanctity of the monument are not
 affected in any way.
(Recommendation at Para 24)
18.   The monuments like Taj Mahal, Agra and Sun Temple at Konark which are famous all over the world and
 attract millions of tourists to the country should be conserved/preserved  very carefully and the Archaeological
 Survey of India should pay utmost attention towards this. The Committee recommends the Department to make
 adequate budgetary provision for this purpose. The Committee also recommends that the findings of the expert
 Committee on Konark Sun Temple should be implemented immediately in order to enable this famous
 monument survive.
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT
19.   Though the budgetary allocation of the Archaeological Survey of India has increased over the period, the available
 allocations are always inadequate to meet the demand of conservation and preservation of the ancient monuments.
 Archaeological Survey of India provides maximum allocation for the important monuments like Taj Mahal, Agra and
 Sun Temple, Konark, which are visited by large number of tourists from all over the world. However, there is an
 overall shortage of funds for the conservation of other centrally protected monuments.
20.   Archaeological Survey of India has constituted an Expert Committee for making detailed study of the structural
 issues at Sun Temple, Konark. The services of CBRI, Roorkee has already been availed. Archaeological Survey of
 India would ensure that the recommendations of the Expert Committee and the CBRI are fully implemented.
FURTHER RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATION OF THE COMMITTEE
21.   The Committee is constrained to note that Government failed to meet the requirement of funds necessary
 for conservation and preservation of centrally protected monuments and recommends that the Department of
 Culture should continue raising its demand for adequate resource allocation for protection of all monuments of
 national importance.

(Recommendation at Para 29)
22.   The Committee agrees with the Department that Museum security is the major area of concern and
 therefore enhancement of security arrangements is very much required. The Committee while recognizing the
 importance of security arrangements of National Museum also recommends that adequate steps should be taken
 to enhance the security of the State Museums also. The Committee considers that the cut imposed by the Finance
 Ministry at RE stage is unreasonable due to which modernization project of major museums in the country had
 to be postponed and some major international exhibitions planed during the year could not be
organised and recommends the Department to take up the matter with the Finance Ministry to avoid such cuts in
 future.
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT
23.   The recommendations of the Security Committee constituted by the Ministry of Culture have been communicated
 to all State Governments to help them upgrade the security of their Museums. A provision has been made in the
 Ministry’s Scheme for ”Promotion and Strengthening of Regional and Local Museums” for grant of financial assistance
 to State Government Museums to purchase equipment for Security System from 2005-06.

NATIONAL ARCHIVES OF INDIA
(Recommendation at Para 32)
24. The Committee appreciate that the National Archives has undertaken computerization programme in a big
 way. However, the Committee is simultaneously disappointed about the fact that no much attempt has been
 made to acquire documents/manuscripts in the post independence era. The Committee expressed its dismay that
 despite being pointed out by the Committee earlier the Department of Culture has also failed to fill-up the post
 of Director-General of Achieves. The Committee once again recommends that this post should be filled up
 without any further delay.

 Undertakings. In order to improve the acquisition, special meetings were held with the concerned officers of the various
 Ministries to ascertain the practical difficulties involved. Special steps were initiated to shift the records to NAI.
 Besides, special meetings were held with the Public Sector Undertakings and Central Government offices located at
 Mumbai, Bangalore , Kolkata, Chennai and Hyderabad to chalk out plans for early declassification and subsequent
 transfer of public records to the NAI. As a result of these steps, there has been steady improvement in the acquisition of
 records during the year 2005-06 as well as the current year.
26.   The post of the Director General, NAI was advertised by the UPSC and interviews were held. However UPSC did
 not recommend any name. Subsequently the post was again advertised. The last date for receiving the applications is
 over and UPSC is expected to conduct the interview soon. It is hoped that UPSC will select a suitable candidate for the
 post.
FURTHER RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATION OF THE COMMITTEE

 Government sources. Whereas, the Department of Culture has not given any information on acquisition of
 ancient manuscripts and other documents which are still in the private hands and are facing the threat of
 extinction. The Committee, therefore, strongly recommends that NAI should attempt to acquire more and more
 manuscripts/documents and take steps for their preservation.
28.   The Committee is however, constrained to note that there is no progress in the matter of filling up the post
 of Director General, NAI. The Committee fails to understand as to what short of recruitment conditions have
 been framed that no candidate is available for the post fulfilling such conditions. The Committee, recommend
 that recruitment conditions be relaxed or modified to make them realistic so that the post of Director-General,
 NAI is filled up at the earliest so that the functioning of the premier Achieves is not affected.

 Rammohun Roy Library and Delhi Public Library play a crucial role. The Committee recommends that the
 budgetary allocation made for these libraries should be spent in a time bound manner. The Committee further
 recommends that the Delhi Public Library should widen its scope of activities and timely purchases should be

30.   The Annual Action Plan of National Library, Raja Rammohun Roy Library Foundation and Delhi Public Library

 Foundation, Kolkata  has drawn and adopted a new formula for assisting the libraries under their matching scheme.
 According to this new formula the libraries in developed States would get State and Central assistance in the ratio of
 50:50 and those in developing and backward States excluding North-Eastern States the ratio of RRRLF and State

REPORT
        This Report of the Committee deals with the Action Taken by the Government on the observations/
 recommendations as contained in its One Hundred and Fourth Report on Demands for Grants (2006-07) (Demand No.
 92) of the Department of Tourism, which was presented to the Parliament on 22nd May, 2006.

2.     Action Taken Replies have been received from the Government on 21st September, 2006 in respect of all the
 observations/recommendations contained in the Report. These have been categorized as follows:-
              (i)      Recommendations/observations that have been accepted by the Government:
                       Para Nos. 12, 18, 27, 32, 50, 51, 69, 70, 83, 89 and 97                                                    Total-11
              (ii)     Recommendations/observations which the Committee does not desire to pursue in view of the Government replies:
                       Para Nos. 41, 55, 57 and 58                                                                                            Total-4
              (iii)    Recommendations/observations in respect of which replies of the Government have not been accepted by the Committee:
                       Para Nos. 8, 37 and 122                                                                                                  Total-3
              (iv)    Recommendations/ observations in respect of which final replies of the Government are still awaited:
                       Para Nos. 21, 26, 75, 78, 93, 103, 110 and 121                                                                 Total-8
3.     The Committee desires that final replies in respect of the recommendations, which have been categorized as
 interim replies by the Committee should be furnished to it at the earliest.
4.     On scrutiny of the said Action Taken Replies, the Committee has made observations on each item of the action
 taken/proposed to be taken by the Department of Tourism. The recommendations of the Committee contained in the
 One Hundred and Fourth Report, action taken thereon by the Government and recommendations/observations of the
 Committee on each item of action taken have been given in the succeeding paragraphs.
APPROACH IN THE TENTH FIVE YEAR PLAN AND ANALYSIS OF THE ANNUAL PLAN 
 2006-07
(Recommendation at Para 8)
5.     The Committee notes that the plan allocation of Rs. 786 crore of Department of Tourism was not subjected
 to any reduction at RE stage during 2005-06. However, the Committee notes that during the year 2005-06, out of
 the budgeted allocation of Rs. 786 crore, the Department could spend Rs. 552.71 crore upto December, 2005 and
 the same was recouped to Rs. 772 crore by the end of the financial year 2005-06, which clearly indicates the poor
 fiscal management in the Department of Tourism. The Committee, disapproves the tendency of spending funds
 desperately towards the end of the financial year especially, in the months of February and March. The
 Committee expects that the maximum amount of plan outlay would be utilized suitably and substantially during
 the first five months of the financial year so that the Department will be in a position to make demand for more
 allocation of funds at RE stage for implementation of various projects/schemes for development of tourism
 infrastructure and promotion of tourism in the country. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the
 Department should evolve some mechanism of uniform utilization pattern throughout the year so as to avoid
 incurring expenditure at the fag end of the financial year.
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT
6.     Out of the plan allocation of Rs.786.00 crore for the year 2005-06, almost 47 per cent was meant for
 Product/Infrastructure development for Destination and Circuits. The Department of Tourism grants CFA for
 implementation of tourism infrastructure development projects prioritized in consultation with the State/UT
 Governments. In addition, funds are also released for the on-going projects based on receipt of Utilization
 Certificates/Completion Certificates furnished by the concerned State/UT Governments. There is normally delay in
 getting the project proposals complete in all respects and also the UC/CC from the State/UT Governments resulting into
 less utilization of funds in the first three quarters of the financial year. The preparation of the detailed project proposals,
 feasibility reports and identification of land for the projects are time consuming process, however, in order to avoid this
 the concerned State/UT Governments have been requested to submit proposals well in time to have uniformity in
 expenditure throughout the year. In addition to the release of funds for infrastructure development projects, more
 expenditure are also being incurred for settlement of bills of field offices in India and abroad. However, the Department
 of Tourism has utilized 94.19 per cent of the budget allocation of the financial year 2005-06.
FURTHER RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATION OF THE COMMITTEE
7.     The Committee was not satisfied with the replies of the Department of Tourism for poor utilization of funds
 in the first three quarters of the financial year. The Committee feels that the reasons put-forth by the
 Department of Tourism are routine in nature and remedial measures may be taken in advance. The Committee
 therefore, recommends the Department of Tourism that some fool-proof method be devised for having
 uniformity in expenditure throughout the year and State/UT Governments may also be impressed upon for
 timely submission of project proposals and utilization certificates/completion certificates for release of funds
 through central financial assistance. The Committee is also surprised to note that the ATR have been furnished

PARLIAMENT OF INDIA
file:///C/Users/user/Desktop/pri/Committee%20on%20Transport,%20Tourism%20and%20Culture/113.htm[28-08-2018 13:23:58]
 to the Committee on 21st September, 2006 and yet it does not contain any information about actual number of
 project proposals received in time, how many are pending for consideration and how many
 utilization/completion certificates were issued thereon.
(Recommendation at Para 12)
8.     Taking into account the Actual Expenditure of 2002-03 to 2004-05 and Anticipated Expenditure of 2005-06
 and BE of 2006-07, the Department of Tourism has been allocated approximate 91 per cent of the total outlay of
 Rs.2900 crore for the Tenth Five Year Plan. The Committee notes that the outlay for the annual plan 2006-07 is
 Rs. 830 crore which is short by Rs. 259 crore of the total budgeted outlay of Rs. 2900 crore for the Tenth Plan.
 The committee is of the view that the plan outlay is insufficient to explore the tourism potential available in the
 country and the Department of Tourism has not been allocated the budgeted outlay judiciously. The Committee
 feels that the financial requirement of the Department of Tourism is much more and expects that the plan outlay
 of the Department would be increased in the coming years. The Committee expects that Department of Tourism
 will also be able to utilize the enhanced allocation for effective implementation of the schemes/programmes for
 development and promotion of tourism and also for creating world class and dependable tourism product and
 infrastructure required for sustained and structured growth of tourism. The Committee recommends that while
 revising allocations, due consideration should be given to the actual expenditure incurred in the past. This way,
 the Department of Tourism will be in a position to make demand for more allocation of funds at RE stage.
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT
9.     The Department of Tourism had requested the Planning Commission for an enhanced need based allocation of Rs.
 1410 crore for the year 2006-07. The Planning Commission has finally approved an allocation of Rs.830 crore for the
 tourism sector considering various factors and inter-se priority. It is expected that the enhanced allocation of funds for
 the year 2006-07 will be utilized for effective implementation of the schemes/programmes of the Department of
 Tourism which includes mainly development of tourism infrastructure to world class standard.
FURTHER RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATION OF THE COMMITTEE
10.   The Committee notes the reply and hopes that the plan outlay of the Department of Tourism would be
 increased so that the vast tourism potential available in the country could be exploited optimally to create world
 class and dependable tourism product and infrastructure.
PRODUCT/INFRASTRUCTURE DEVELOPMENT
(a)    Major Destination and Circuits Development
(Recommendation at Para 18)
11.   The Committee is happy to note that Department of Tourism has been able to spend the entire amount
 available for development of infrastructure. The Committee is also happy to note that the Department of
 Tourism has finally decided to concentrate on major destinations and major circuits as was being stressed by the
 Committee for long. The Committee agrees with the Department that amount of Rs. 8 crore per circuit and Rs. 5
 crore per destination is insufficient and recommends that the amount should be increased to Rs. 50 crore as
 suggested by the Department of Tourism. The Committee notes that the Department of Tourism has modified
 the pattern of funding to enable all States for improving the existing products and developing new tourism
 products of world class standard. Now 100 per cent assistance is provided to State Governments/UTs for
 creation of infrastructure and other promotional projects and the State Governments have to provide mainly
 land and external infrastructure. The Committee is of the view that if India has to realise its enormous potential
 in tourism, then it must provide exclusive world-class tourism products and destination to compete successfully
 with other Asian tourism markets and the scope and reach of domestic tourism should also be broadened
 through the development of competitive destinations. The Committee also observes that arrival for foreign
 tourists is only 3.46 million, which is much less, in comparison to other countries in the world. The Committee,
 therefore, recommends the Department of Tourism to develop competitive destinations that match international
 standards in terms of price, quality and satisfy the national and international travellers. Aggressive marketing
 efforts and publicity should be given to these destinations in order to create a niche market for Indian tourism
 products as well as to attract more tourists to these destinations. The critical infrastructural gaps can be bridged
 by creating a tourism development fund for augmenting larger flow of funds for development of tourism
 infrastructure. The Committee also recommends the Department of Tourism to create awareness about the
 environment impacts of tourism with regard to the carrying capacity of tourist destinations.
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT
12.   As recommended by the Committee, the Department of Tourism is exploring the possibilities to increase the

PARLIAMENT OF INDIA
file:///C/Users/user/Desktop/pri/Committee%20on%20Transport,%20Tourism%20and%20Culture/113.htm[28-08-2018 13:23:58]
 Foreign Tourist Traffic to India from the existing figures to 25 million in ten years time for which the work to prepare
 action plan has been entrusted to M/s. AC Nielsen ORG-MARG Pvt. Ltd, New Delhi. The Department of Tourism is
 concentrating on improvement/development of existing as well as new tourism infrastructure to world standard for
 which it is proposed to increase the central financial assistance to State/UT Governments to Rs.25 crore and Rs.50 crore
 for development of tourist destination and tourism circuits respectively.
13.   World class tourism infrastructure projects requires very large investment this may not be possible out of the
 budgetary resources of the Government of India alone. It is, therefore, proposed to promote large revenue generating
 projects for development of tourism infrastructure in public-private partnerships and in partnerships with other
 Government/Semi-Government agencies.
14.   For bridging the critical infrastructure gaps for the tourist infrastructure at the important destinations, the Ministry
 of Finance has already initiated schemes like Viability-Gap-Funding (VGF) which also include tourism projects.
 Aggressive marketing in the print and electronic media and also through internet campaigns has also been launched for
 augmenting the tourist traffic from the abroad market to India.
15.   The recommendations of the Committee is appreciative for creating awareness about the environmental
 impacts of tourism with regard to the carrying capacity of tourist destinations.
FURTHER RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATION OF THE COMMITTEE
16.   The Committee notes that the Department of Tourism is concentrating on improvement/ development of
 existing as well as new tourism products to world class standards for which the Government has proposed to
 increase the central financial assistance to State/Union Territory for development of tourism destinations and
 circuits in the country. The Committee is of the opinion that if the country has to improve its vast tourism
 potential to world class standard, it requires larger flow of funds for development of infrastructure both from
 Government and private sector. The Committee, therefore, recommends the Government to explore the
 possibilities for creating and promoting the tourism infrastructure projects in public-private partnership and
 approach the Ministry of Finance for releasing funds for bridging the infrastructure gap at important
 destinations besides resorting to aggressive marketing of tourism products through print and electronic media.
 World wide web campaigns should also be launched for augmenting incoming tourist traffic flow from abroad.
(Recommendation at Para 21)
17.   The Committee notes that the major constraint in the expansion of international tourist traffic to India is
 non-availability of adequate infrastructure including accessibility to tourist destinations and cultural/heritage
 sites. The Committee is deeply concerned over the poor road connectivity of tourist destinations and circuits and
 cultural heritage sites. The Committee notes that Department of Tourism is also seized with the matter and
 appreciates the efforts taken by Department of Tourism for improvement of better road connectivity to these
 sites. The Committee observes that many of the tourist destinations are away from the National Highways and
 lack road connectivity of desired standard. The Committee recommends that Ministry of Shipping, Road
 Transport and Highways must be impressed about the proper road connectivity of all important destinations
 and circuits. However, preference may be given to World Heritage Sites and Buddhist Circuits where most of
 the tourists in general and foreign tourists in particular, visit every year. In this regard the Committee agrees to
 the suggestions of the Department of Tourism for making available fund from Central Road Funds.
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT
18.   The matter has already been taken up with the Ministry of Shipping, Road Transport and Highways to improve the
 connectivity to the important tourist destinations including World Heritage Sites, Buddhist Sites through Central Road
 Fund Scheme of the Ministry of Shipping, Road Transport and Highways.
FURTHER RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATION OF THE COMMITTEE
19.   The Committee notes that the Department of Tourism is taking up the matter with the Ministry of Shipping,
 Road Transport & Highways for improving the connectivity to the important tourist destinations including
 World Heritage Sites, Buddhist Sites through Central Road Fund Scheme. The Committee recommends the
 Department of Tourism to pursue vigourously the matter with the Ministry of Shipping, Road Transport &
 Highways. The Committee also desires the Department of Tourism to inform the Committee about the progress
 in the matter.
(Recommendation at Para 26)
20.   The Committee regrets to note that a large number of tourism projects sanctioned to State Governments/
 UTs by the Department of Tourism during the Eighth, Ninth and Tenth Five Year Plan are still incomplete.
 During Eight and Ninth Plans, 2526 projects were sanctioned and out of this only 1761 projects got completed
 and balance 765 projects remained incomplete for one reason or the others. The progress of work with regard to
 the Tenth Plan period is also not very satisfactory. Out of the 895 projects sanctioned, only 276 projects got

PARLIAMENT OF INDIA
file:///C/Users/user/Desktop/pri/Committee%20on%20Transport,%20Tourism%20and%20Culture/113.htm[28-08-2018 13:23:58]
 completed and there still remained a shortfall of 619 projects. The Committee is apprehensive that with this slow
 pace of work the Department of Tourism will not be able to achieve the physical and financial targets. The
 Committee is of the view that Department of Tourism has failed to activate the State Government machinery
 which have resulted in such a huge mismatch in terms of projections and achievements. The Committee feels
 that if these projects were not completed in a definite time frame, then, the entire taxpayers money will go waste.
 In this regard, the active participation and support of the state Government is essential for tourism to bloom and
 spread its numerous benefits among the host population. The Committee recommends the Department of
 Tourism to prioritize the projects and seek active support of the State Governments/UTs for the completion of
 the remaining tourism projects so as to avoid delay in the implementation of the projects as well as cost overrun.
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT
21.   The Department of Tourism has been requesting the State Governments to submit completion certificates for
 pending projects. However, out of the sanctioned projects of the Eighth and Ninth Plans, 1830 projects have been
 completed as on date. Similarly, 285 projects of the Tenth Plan have been completed. The numbers of the completed
 projects could further increase on receipt of the information regarding completion of the projects and receipt of the
 completion certificates from the State Governments.
22.   The State Governments were impressed upon the need for full utilization of the funds sanctioned. The State
 Governments were informed that no more funds would be released for the projects of Eighth Plan period which are now
 pending. These projects are to be completed by the respective State Governments. They were also informed that no
 funds would be released after 31.3.2006 for any pending projects of the Ninth plan.
23.   In order to seek active support of the State Governments/UTs for the completion of the remaining tourism projects
 so as to avoid delay in the implementation of the projects as well as cost overrun, all the State Governments have been
 apprised of the apprehensions of the Committee and also to complete the pending projects.
FURTHER RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATION OF THE COMMITTEE
24.   The Committee is constrained to note that out of the 2526 sanctioned projects during Eighth and Ninth Five
 Year Plan periods, only 1830 projects have been completed as on date. Similarly, out of the 895 sanctioned
 projects during the Tenth Five Year Plan only 285 projects have since been completed. The Committee feels that
 there is lack of co-ordination and monitoring of projects between the Department of Tourism and State/UT
 Governments and this needs to be strengthened and in the future corrective measures may be taken so that more
 and more sanctioned projects may be completed in time.
(Recommendation at Para 27)
25.   The Committee notes with dissatisfaction that Department of Tourism has not evolved effective system or
 planning to systematically anticipate the actual requirement of funds otherwise, the investments could have
 yielded commensurating results. The Committee feels that strict monitoring is crucial for timely completion of
 any project and recommends that the monitoring agency should play rather proactive role and do away with the
 procedural hurdles for timely completion of these pending projects so that the budgeted allocation is utilized
 optimally and utilization certificates are issued in time. The Committee directs the Department to inform the
 Committee about the progress in the matter.
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT
26.   The Department of Tourism was allocated Rs.2900.00 crore in the Tenth Five Year Plan, out of which Rs.2716
 crore has been allocated so far in various Annual Plan allocations by Ministry of Finance after taking into consideration
 various factors. 1830 projects have been completed, out of the sanctioned projects of the Eighth and Ninth Plans and
 285 projects of the Tenth Plan as on date. The numbers of the completed projects could further increase on receipt of
 the information regarding completion of the projects and receipt of the completion certificates from the State
 Governments.
27.   The Department of Tourism is extending financial assistance to State/UT Governments for development of tourism
 infrastructure which are generally one tourist circuit and two destinations, prioritized in consultation with them. The
 progress of implementation of the projects sanctioned are done by the Department at the level of Secretary (Tourism)
 and the same is also done at the level of the Secretary (Tourism) of the concerned State/UT Government from time to
 time. The domestic offices of Department of Tourism is also actively involved in the monitoring of these projects. The
 State Governments were informed that no more funds would be released for the projects of Eight Plan period which are
 now pending. These projects are to be completed by the respective State Governments. They were also informed that no
 funds would be released after 31.3.2006 for any pending projects of the Ninth plan. The Secretary (Tourism) has also
 impressed upon other implementing agencies like ITDC, CPWD, ASI etc. to be pro­active in completion of the
 respective projects well in time.

PARLIAMENT OF INDIA
file:///C/Users/user/Desktop/pri/Committee%20on%20Transport,%20Tourism%20and%20Culture/113.htm[28-08-2018 13:23:58]
FURTHER RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATION OF THE COMMITTEE
28.   The Committee notes the reply and recommends the Department of Tourism to have close co-ordination
 with the implementing agencies viz., ITDC, CPWD, ASI etc., for timely completion of tourism projects. This way
 the Department of Tourism will not only achieve the physical and financial targets but also help in
 creation/improvement of tourism infrastructure.
(b)    Rural Tourism
(Recommendation at Para 32)
29.   The Committee notes that the concept of Rural Tourism is the new emerging area under
 product/infrastructure and destination development scheme and aim to promote village tourism to spread
 tourism and its social-economic benefits to rural and its remote geographic regions. The Committee feels that
 rural tourism need to be given impetus by earmarking funds for projects on the basis of a model plan for each
 State for the purpose and these villages should be taken up for priority development and linked with the
 restoration of heritage properties in the area. The Committee is of the opinion that this would provide boost to
 local performing arts and help conserve the local culture apart from preventing rural-urban migration. The
 Committee recommends that local people in the rural areas should be encouraged to participate in tourism
 related projects in order to provide employment opportunity and to increase the income level in the rural areas.
 The Committee also recommends that proper training should be imparted on improvement of environment,
 hygiene and sanitation etc. as coordinated effort to develop rural tourism infrastructure.
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT
30.   The creation of infrastructure in Rural areas having potential for tourism is being supported under the existing
 scheme of Product/Infrastructure Development for Destination and Circuit of Ministry of Tourism, while community
 participation and the capacity building including skill upgradation in such rural areas are being supported through GoI-
UNDP Endogenous Tourism Project and Scheme of Capacity Building for service providers.
31.   In this connection, the Ministry of Tourism has already identified 25 villages in consultation and interaction with
 the State/UT Governments for development as Rural Tourism sites during the year  2006-07 for spreading the attributes
 of Indian Art and Culture within and outside the country, thereby enabling the visitor to gain first hand experience of
 diverse art and craft skills at the various rural tourism sites and generating further tourist arrivals.
32.   The promotion of rural tourism can lead to increased tourist arrivals to rural sites and in the process can strengthen
 rural livelihoods including benefit to the youth, through income from visitor handling services apart from income
 through art and craft activities.
FURTHER RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATION OF THE COMMITTEE
33.   The Committee notes that the Department of Tourism is making efforts to boost rural tourism
 infrastructure in the country. The Committee also notes that during 2006-07, the Department of Tourism has
 already identified 25 villages in consultation with the State/UT Governments for development of rural tourism
 sites in the country. The Committee expects that the promotion of rural tourism can lead to increased tourist
 arrivals to rural sites and in the process can strengthen rural livelihoods including benefit to the youth through
 income from visitor handling services apart from income through art and craft activities.
ASSISTANCE FOR LARGE REVENUE GENERATING PROJECTS
(Recommendation at Para 37)
34.   The Committee notes that the Department of Tourism is providing support in the form of grant to Large
 Revenue Generating Projects through the financial institutions and tourism finance corporations. It also notes
 that 10 projects like Tourist Trains, Cruise Vessels, Cruise Terminals, Convention Centres, Golf Courses etc.
 have been sanctioned by the Department of Tourism under the scheme. The Committee expects that these
 projects would be completed within the stipulated time-frame though no target, therefore, have been
 communicated to the Committee. The Committee is constrained to note that only amount of Rs. 9.28 crore could
 be spent by the end of December, 2005. The Committee hopes that the Department will be able to utilize the
 amount of Rs. 30 crore allocated for the current year. However, the Committee feels that the allocation is
 meager when grants-in-aid for one project itself can go upto 50 crore. The Committee feels that there is a need
 for higher level of participation by the private sector in all the stages of the tourism development as the growth
 in tourism sector can only be achieved by major flow of investments coming in from private sector and public
 investments can act as a catalyst. The Committee recommends that private sector investment should be
 enhanced by removing the impediments to the growth of tourism and expediting policy support. The proposal
 for inclusion of special trains like “Palace on Wheels” and “Deccan Odyssey” should also be considered in
 collaboration with the concerned State Governments for improving the connectivity and urban infrastructure in
 Buddhist sites. The Committee also recommends that while identifying the projects under the public-private

PARLIAMENT OF INDIA
file:///C/Users/user/Desktop/pri/Committee%20on%20Transport,%20Tourism%20and%20Culture/113.htm[28-08-2018 13:23:58]
 participation, the strategy for removing regional imbalances should also be taken care of.
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT
35.   During the year 2005-06, the Department of Tourism did not receive suitable large revenue generating projects
 from the State/UT Governments. Only Rs.9.30 crore could be utilized in this regard and the balance funds available
 under this head were re-appropriated for development of tourism infrastructure. In the meantime, Expression of
 Interests were invited for Large revenue generating tourism projects which are to be implemented in public-private
 partnerships and once the guidelines are finalized, suitable projects will be considered for implementation.
36.   The Development of world class tourism infrastructure in the country, with the help of private sector participation
 is being actualized by attracting their techno-managerial efficiencies and investments under the scheme of Assistance to
 Large Revenue Generating Projects of the Ministry. The revision of the scheme is under consideration to ensure higher-
level participation of the private sector in tourism development in the country. Under the scope of the scheme, projects
 of tourist trains also qualify for assistance for which the State Governments/concerned agencies have to come forward
 with suitable projects.
FURTHER RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATION OF THE COMMITTEE
37.   The Committee notes that the Department of Tourism is formulating the guidelines to ensure higher level of
 participation of the private sector in the development of tourism in the country. However, the Committee is
 constrained to note that the Department of Tourism could not utilize the allocation during the year 2006-07 for
 want of suitable large revenue generating projects from the State/UT Governments. The Committee
 recommends that the Department of Tourism should be more cautious while identifying and selecting the
 projects and in any case appropriation of allocation should not be done and State/UT Governments should be
 persuaded for coming forward with suitable project for sustained and structured tourism growth in the country.
CAPACITY BUILDING FOR SERVICE PROVIDERS
(Recommendation at Para 41)
38.   The Committee notes with dismay that there is a heavy shortfall in the utilization of funds allocated under
 the head “Capacity Building for Service Providers” and the Department of Tourism has not furnished any
 reasons for under utilization of funds. It appears to the Committee that while revising allocation, little
 consideration has been paid to the actual expenditure incurred in the past and expects the Department of
 Tourism to utilize the funds more judiciously during 2006-07. The Committee notes that the Capacity Building
 for Service Providers Scheme provides training through one to five day modules to persons who are working in
 unorganized sectors and who come into contact with a large number of tourists like those working in small
 hotels, dhabas, ticketing agents, travel agencies, police personnel etc. The Committee desires the Department of
 Tourism to prepare broad framework for the countrywide training programme to develop Human Resource and
 place them with important groups of service providers engaged in the tourism industry.      
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT
39.   The ‘Capacity Building for Service Providers’ (CBSP) scheme was launched in 2002-03 and was initially aimed at
 imparting training of tourism awareness for 1-5 days only by limited Implementing Agencies in the Central/State

 Government has introduced medical visa to facilitate foreign tourists coming to India for medical treatment. The
 Committee hopes that low cost of medical treatment, high level of expertise and varied system of medicines of
 India are factors that can lead to a boost in health tourism in the country.
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT
88.   On Tourism Ministry’s request, Ministry of Home Affairs has introduced a new category of “Medical Visa” (‘M’-
Visa), which can be given for specific purpose to foreign tourists coming to India for medical treatment. The initial
 period for such visa may be upto a period of one year or the period of treatment whichever is less, which can be
 extended for a further period upto one year by the State Government/FRROs on the production of a medical certificate
 from the concerned specialized hospitals in the country and can be further extended by Ministry of Home Affairs only
 on the recommendation of the State Government/FRROs supported by appropriate medical documents. Co-terminus
 with the patient ‘MX’ Visa is granted to spouse or blood relations of the patient coming to India for medical treatment.
89.   For providing easy access of medical aid to the visiting tourists include  preparation of a guide on select Indian
 cities and corresponding hospitals, and a guide on suggested uniform price-band for different specialty services for
 Indian hospitals by Indian Healthcare Federation, a Non-Governmental Organization affiliated to the Confederation of
 Indian Industry for promoting Health Tourism. Medical and health facilities available in India have been promoted at
 various international platforms such as World Travel Mart, London and ITB Berlin etc. for medical tourists.
FURTHER RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATION OF THE COMMITTEE
90.   The Committee notes that the Ministry of Home Affairs has introduced a new category of medical visa for
 specific purpose to foreign tourists coming to India for medical treatment and the period of visa may vary
 depending upon the medical procedure. The Committee recommends the Department of Tourism to draw
 special packages for medical tourists and provide more concessions to the tourists coming for medical treatment
 in India.
BEACH TOURISM
(Recommendation at Para 103)
91.   The Committee notes that the concept of Beach Tourism is fast emerging and growing in the country. The
 Committee observe that for development of beach tourism, the Department of Tourism has extended the
 financial support to a number of sites on the west coast of India and a study for an integrated sustainable
 development of coastal tourism in the States of West Bengal, Orissa and Andhra Pradesh has already been
 undertaken and a comprehensive coastal tourism policy for these States is under consideration. The Committee
 feels that development of beach tourism along the coastal lines of the country will certainly give impetus to the
 cruise tourism and recommends the Department of tourism to identify and develop more beaches both on the
 West and East coast in the country with active participation by private sector and due publicity should be given
 for developing these beaches as a major tourist attraction.
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT
92.   Ministry of Tourism extends financial assistance for tourism infrastructure development of specified tourism
 projects including projects related to each tourism, tourist spots of States/Union Territories and procurement of cruise
 vessels, boats etc. for promotion of beach and cruise tourism. Ministry of Tourism has also given No Objection
 Certificate to two private operators to operate their cruise vessels for the purpose of cruise tourism promotion along the
 Indian coast.
93.   In addition to above, a High Power Steering Group has been constituted to formulate Cruise Shipping policy for the
 country. On the recommendations of this Steering Group, a Working Group has been constituted by Department of
 Shipping for identification of Ports having cruise tourism potential along the East and West Coast of India.

FURTHER RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATION OF THE COMMITTEE
94.   The Committee notes that the Department of Tourism is extending financial assistance for tourism
 infrastructure development including projects related to beach tourism, tourist spots of States/Union Territories
 and procurement of cruise vessels, boats etc. for promotion of beach and cruise tourism and two private
 operators are operating their cruise vessels for the purpose of cruise tourism promotion along the Indian coast.
 The Committee notes with dissatisfaction that the High Power Steering Group which was constituted to
 formulate cruise shipping policy for the country resulted nothing in concrete but led to the formation of another
 Working Group only. Therefore, the Committee recommends the Department of Tourism to impress upon the
 Department of Shipping for finalization of the cruise shipping policy for integrated and sustainable development
 of coastal tourism in the country.
ADVENTURE TOURISM
(Recommendation at Para 110)
95.   The Committee notes that geographical diversity of our country provides opportunities for out door and
 adventure sports activities for all tastes and interests and every level of experience. The Committee also notes
 that major adventure tourism activities range from trekking and skiing in the Himalayas, river rafting along the
 Ganges, water sports in Goa, trout fishing in Himachal Pradesh and U.P., Heli skiing in Himachal Pradesh and
 wind surfing, scuba diving and yatching in the Andaman and Lakshadweep Island. The Committee feels that
 there is need for regulation and promotion in the country of adventure tourism products. The Committee
 therefore, recommends the Department of Tourism to better regulate the adventure tourism products, specially
 the mountain based and water sports adventure activities amongst the youth and introduce the minimum
 standards of safety and conservation for tour operators.
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT
96.   The suggestion of the Hon’ble Committee is welcomed. There are a vast number of adventure sports activities
 being conducted in the country. In order to ensure safety of participants in such activities the need had been felt to lay
 down the minimum acceptable standards in terms of equipment and human resources. Draft guidelines on Adventure
 Sports/Tourism related activities which have the greatest volumes in terms of participation have also been circulated to
 all States/UT Governments by the Ministry of Tourism to ensure that minimum standards of safety and consideration
 are followed by tour operators while promoting these activities.
FURTHER RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATION OF THE COMMITTEE
97.   The Committees notes that draft guidelines on Adventure Sports/Tourism related activities have been
 circulated to all the States/UT Governments by the Department of Tourism. The Committee recommends the
 Department of Tourism that while finalizing the guidelines due attention will be given to the safety of
 participants besides laying down the minimum acceptable standards in terms of equipment and human
 resources.
DEVELOPMENT OF TOURISM IN NORTH-EASTERN REGION
(Recommendation at Para 121)
98.   The Committee notes the efforts taken by the Department of Tourism for promotion of tourism in the
 North-Eastern States. It also notes that a nation wide special campaign ‘paradise unexplored’ has also been
 launched for promoting and marketing of various tourism products in the North Eastern region. However, the
 Committee is constrained to note that inspite of the concerted efforts of Department of Tourism the flow of
 tourist traffic to these regions are marginal and is being largely hampered by Restricted Area Permit, Protected
 Area Permit and Inner Line Permit and lack of suitable infrastructure and other related facilities and amenities
 in various tourists places in the region. The Committee observes that inspite of incurring a lot of expenditure for
 development of tourism in North-East region no perceptible improvement is seen in the ground situation and
 Department of Tourism has to put lot of efforts to fully explore the tourism potential in the Region. Further, the
 revenue earned from tourism are not estimated by the States. The Committee, therefore, recommends the
 Department of Tourism to prioritize the projects in consultation with the State Government for upgradation and
 creation of infrastructure and destinations in the Region besides addressing the major issues for the growth and
 development of tourism in the Region like mandatory permit system, law and order situation and lack of private
 investment etc. This way, the Department of Tourism will be able to bring the North Eastern Region in the
 mainstream of national development agenda.
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT
99.   The recommendations of the Committee have been noted. The projects for the North-East are prioritized in the

 beginning of the year in consultation with the State Governments keeping in view the requirements of infrastructure
 and tourist flow to the area. The Ministry has been promoting the North East through specific publicity campaigns and
 has also taken up the issue of permits with the Ministry of Home Affairs.
FURTHER RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATION OF THE COMMITTEE
100. The Committee notes that the Department of Tourism is giving priority to the projects for the North-East
 region in consultation with the State Governments keeping in view the requirements of infrastructure and
 tourist flow to the area and is giving publicity to the North-East through specific campaigns. The Committee
 recommends the Department of Tourism to address the major issues like mandatory permit system, law and
 order situation and lack of private investment etc. for the growth and development of tourism in the region.
(Recommendation at Para 122)
101. The Committee also recommends the Department of Tourism to keep an account of the revenue earned
 from tourism in these States as it will give economic benefits of tourism in the form of its contribution to Gross
 Domestic Products (GDP) and employment.
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT
102. Tourism being an amalgam of a variety of economic activities such as Hotels and Restaurants, Air
 Road/Rail/Water Transport, Entertainment services, services of Travel Agencies/Transport Operators, etc., the
 estimation of the economic benefits of tourism in terms of its contribution to the GDP and employment is based on the
 methodology of Tourism Satellite Accounts recommended by the World Tourism Organization (WTO). In India,
 Tourism Satellite Accounts (TSA) have been prepared for the country as a whole for the first time for the year 2002-03
 through a study commissioned by the Ministry of Tourism. Development of TSA is a complicated process. The WTO
 has been considering preparation of TSA at Regional Level for some time but no methodology could be evolved by
 them so far. Issue has been discussed by them at various international conferences and workshops without much
 success. Further, development of TSA is linked with the system of National Accounting at the National Level and
 system of State Income at the State Level. As such till such time a firm methodology is available for development of
 TSA at Regional Level, it may not be possible to develop the TSA for States.
FURTHER RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATION OF THE COMMITTEE
103. The Committee understands the problem of the Department of Tourism in estimation of the economic
 benefits of tourism in terms of its contribution to the GDP and employment on the basis of Tourism Satellite
 Accounting System and recommends the Department of Tourism to carry on its efforts to evolve a methodology
 for Tourism Satellite Accounts at regional level for keeping an account of the revenue earned from tourism in
 that State.

        The Committee desires that final replies in respect of the recommendations, which have been categorized as

APPROACH IN THE TENTH FIVE YEAR PLAN AND ANALYSIS OF THE ANNUAL PLAN 
 2006-07
        The Committee was not satisfied with the replies of the Department of Tourism for poor utilization of funds
 in the first three quarters of the financial year. The Committee feels that the reasons put-forth by the
 Department of Tourism are routine in nature and remedial measures may be taken in advance. The Committee
 therefore, recommends the Department of Tourism that some fool proof method be devised for having
 uniformity in expenditure throughout the year and State/UT Governments may also be impressed upon for
 timely submission of project proposals and utilization certificates/completion certificates for release of funds
 through central financial assistance. The Committee is also surprised to note that the ATR have been furnished
 to the Committee on 21st September 2006 and yet it does not contain any information about actual number of
 project proposals received in time, how many are pending for consideration and how many
 utilization/completion certificates were issued thereon.
        The Committee notes the reply and hopes that the plan outlay of the Department of Tourism would be
 increased so that the vast tourism potential available in the country could be exploited optimally to create world
 class and dependable tourism product and infrastructure.                                                                      
                                                                                                                                            (Paras 7 and 10)
PRODUCT/INFRASTRUCTURE DEVELOPMENT
(a)    Major Destination and Circuit Development
        The Committee notes that the Department of Tourism is concentrating on improvement/ development of
 existing as well as new tourism products to world-class standards for which the Government has proposed to
 increase the Central financial assistance to State/ Union Territory for development of tourism destinations and
 circuits in the country. The Committee is of the opinion that if the country has to improve its vast tourism
 potential to world class standard, it requires larger flow of funds for development of infrastructure both from
 Government and private sector. The Committee therefore, recommends the Government to explore the
 possibilities for creating and promoting the tourism infrastructure projects in public-private partnership and
 approach the Ministry of Finance for releasing funds for bridging the infrastructure gap at important
 destinations besides resorting to aggressive marketing of tourism products through print and electronic media.
 World wide web campaigns should also be launched for augmenting incoming tourist traffic flow from abroad.
        The Committee notes that the Department of Tourism is taking up the matter with the Ministry of Shipping,
 Road Transport and Highways for improving the connectivity to the important tourist destinations including
 World Heritage Sites, Buddhist Sites through Central Road Fund Scheme. The Committee recommends the
 Department of Tourism to pursue vigourously the matter with the Ministry of Shipping, Road, Transport and
 Highways. The Committee also desires the Department of Tourism to inform the Committee about the progress
 in the matter.
        The Committee is constrained to note that out of the 2526 sanctioned projects during Eight and Ninth Five
 Year Plan periods only 1830 projects have been completed as on date. Similarly, out of the 895 sanctioned
 projects during the Tenth Five Year Plan only 285 projects have since been completed. The Committee feels that
 there is lack of co-ordination and monitoring of projects between the Department of Tourism and State/UT
 Governments and this needs to be strengthened and in the future corrective measures may be taken so that more
 and more sanctioned projects may be completed in time.
        The Committee notes the reply and recommends the Department of Tourism to have close co-ordination
 with the implementing agencies viz., ITDC, CPWD, ASI etc., for timely completion of tourism projects. This way
 the Department of Tourism will not only achieve the physical and financial targets but also help in
 creation/improvement of tourism infrastructure.
                                                                                                                              (Paras 16, 19, 24 and 28)

        The Committee notes that the Department of Tourism is making efforts to boost rural tourism
 infrastructure in the country. The Committee also notes that during 2006-07, the Department of Tourism has

 sites in the country. The Committee expects that the promotion of rural tourism can lead to increased tourist
 arrivals to rural sites and in the process can strengthen rural livelihoods including benefit to the youth through
 income from visitor handling services apart from income through art and craft activities.

            (i)     Recommendations/observations that have been accepted by the Government:
                    Para Nos. 9, 19, 21, 23, 27, 42 and 73                                                                              Total-7
            (ii)    Recommendations/observations which the Committee do not desire to pursue in view of the Government replies:
                    Para Nos. 34 and 39                                                                                                        Total-2

                    Para Nos. 46, 50, 55 and 56                                                                                             Total-4
3.     The Committee desires that final replies in respect of the recommendations, which have been categorized as
 interim replies by the Committee should be furnished to it at the earliest.
4.     On scrutiny of the Action Taken Replies, the Committee has made observations on each item of the action
 taken/proposed to be taken by the Department of Shipping. The recommendations of the Committee contained in the
 One Hundred Fifth Report, action taken thereon by the Government and recommendations/observations of the
 Committee on each item of action taken have been given in the succeeding paragraphs.
ANALYSIS OF ANNUAL PLAN 2006-07
(Recommendation at Para 9)
5. The Committee notes that in the annual plan 2005-06, the outlay of Department of Shipping was reduced from
 Rs.2419.66 crore to Rs.2333.71 crore at RE stage. The reduction had been both in the Gross Budgetary Support
 as well as IEBR component. As far as the reasons for under utilization of funds is concerned, the Committee
 finds that inadequate preparedness on the part of executing authorities and procedural rigidity for approval of
 scheme are main culprits for under utilization of funds. Therefore, the Committee recommends that Department
 of Shipping should not only have to do away the procedural hurdles leading to delay in processing and
 approving the scheme but also have to adopt proactive approach while preparing the scheme. In BE 2006-07, an
 outlay of Rs.3263.19 crore  has been provided which consists of a Gross Budgetary Support of Rs.740.88 crore
 and IEBR of Rs.2522.31 crore , which is almost 40 per cent over and above the amount of Rs.2419.66 crore
 allocated in BE 2005-06. The Committee expects that the increase in the plan outlay will have a positive effect of
 the schemes/projects of the Department of Shipping. The Committee is of the view that complete utilization of
 the enhanced allocation will help effective implementation of the schemes/performance undertaken by the
 Department of Shipping. The Committee recommends that the Government should increase the outlay of
 Department of Shipping and if need be, supplement the allocation by increasing the Gross Budgetary Support to
 the Department of Shipping.
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT
6.     The views and recommendations of the hon’ble Committee are noted.
PORT SECTOR
(Recommendation at Para 15)
7.     The committee is not satisfied with the reasons given by the Department of Shipping for shortfall in the
 utilization of the approved outlay and feels that the reasons could have been anticipated in advance by the
 Department of Shipping, this clearly shows the lack of pro-active approach on the part of the Department. The
 Committee is perturbed to note that there has been a huge shortfall in the utilization of Funds vis-a­-vis
 approved outlay for the Port Sector. In BE 2005-06, an outlay of Rs. 1163.75 crore comprising of Rs.280.24 crore
 Gross Budgetary Support and Rs.883.21 crore IEBR was provided for the Port Sector. As against this, the actual
 expenditure is anticipated to be Rs.668.33 crore . The Committee feels that while proposing the Plan Outlay, the
 Department of Shipping had not done strategic planning and observes that there is a

REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT
8.     The Annual Plan proposal are formulated about five to six months in advance before the commencement of the
 Annual Plan period after factoring in the anticipated expenditure during the current year and the assessed requirements

 anticipated expenditure during the remaining part of the year. This does not necessarily follow a uniform or standard
 pattern every year. In view of the time lag between the formulation  process for Annual Plan and the implementation

 advised that there should be realistic approach while proposing the Annual Plan Outlays and that only token provision
 may be kept for projects for which administrative approval is yet to be accorded by the Competent Authority. A
 monitoring mechanism for regular review of plan expenditure on monthly and quarterly basis has been put in place. In
 the event, if a particular Port/organization is found to be lagging in expenditure vis-a-vis outlay, the reason thereof are
 examined threadbare so that the hurdle in achieving the financial target (budgeted outlay) are sorted out and optimum
 utilization of funds is ensured.
9.     Actual expenditure of the budgetary support component was Rs.217.92 crore against an outlay of Rs.280.54 crore
 (including survey vessels, IT for Department of Shipping, etc.) i.e. 77.68 per cent. If the allocation for survey vessels
 meant for Ministry of Defence  are excluded the actual utilization comes to 94.53 per cent. Hence, there is no major
 shortfall in utilization Gross Budgetary Support (BE) during 2005-06. However, efforts will be made to ensure that
 pace of expenditure picks up further in the next fiscal year.

FURTHER RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATION OF THE COMMITTEE
12.   The Committee notes that there has been a time lag between formulation process for different schemes
 under annual plan and implementation period, due to which, there was a mismatch between the allocation and
 the actual expenditure. The Committee further notes that in order to fill the gap, the Port Trusts have been
 advised to be realistic in approach while proposing the annual plan outlay and only token provision are to be
 kept for projects for which administrative approval is yet to be accorded by the Competent Authority. The
 Department of Shipping has also put into place a monitoring mechanism for regular review of plan expenditure
 on monthly and quarterly basis. The Committee however, does not agree with the contention of the Department
 of Shipping that there is no major shortfall in the utilization of Gross Budgetary Support (BE) during 2005-06,
 and the reasons put forth by the Department are not such which can not be anticipated in advance. The
 Committee, therefore, recommends the Department of Shipping to ensure a more realistic budget and strict
 implementation and monitoring so as to speed up the pace of expenditure during the next fiscal year.
CAPACITY ENHANCEMENT IN MAJOR PORTS
(Recommendation at Para 19)
13.   The Committee notes that the Department of Shipping is implementing the schemes for enhancing the
 capacity and productivity of all major ports and to encourage the private sector participation for the
 development of ports infrastructure and accordingly, comprehensive policy guidelines have been issued. The
 Committee also notes that the Government has allowed cent percent FDI for construction and maintenance of
 ports in order to mobilize substantial resources as well as to improve efficiency, productivity and quality of
 services of Ports. The Committee, however, observed that as against the capacity of 408.60 million TPA, the
 major ports handled a total traffic of 310.80 mt. upto December, 2005. This way, the aggregate capacity of major
 ports exceeds the traffic target marginally. Therefore, there is need to increase capacity of ports on urgent basis.
 The Committee, therefore, recommends the Department of Shipping to take action for development of
 infrastructure in major ports so as to face global competition of sea-borne trade and enhance private sector
 investment including FDI in the sector by addressing the procedural rigidity expediting well integrated and
 coordinated policy framework and approach.
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT
14.   The aggregate cargo handling capacity of the 12 major ports as on 31.3.2006 is 456.20 MT which takes into
 account the addition of berths and improvement in productivity. In 2005-06, the major ports handled traffic of 423.42
 MT. The traffic target in 2006-07 is 465.70 MT. In 2006-07, it is anticipated that three new berths would be
 commissioned which would add a capacity of 26.40 MT thereby taking the capacity of 482.60 MT at the end of 10th
 Plan against the 10th Plan target of 470 MT. Under the National Maritime Development Programme (NMDP)
 formulated by the Department of Shipping, it is planned to augment the aggregate capacity of the major ports to 800.41
 MTPA by 2011-2012. Under the programme , a total 276 projects covering the entire gamut of activities in the major
 ports including berths development, deepening of channels, equipment upgradation, rail/road connectivity and other
 associated activities have been identified which are to be implemented in two phases through Public Private
 Participation (PPP). Out of the total estimated investment of Rs.55,803.73 crore under the scheme, an amount of
 34,505.34 crore is envisaged through private investment including foreign direct investment.
